_comment: Paths in THIS repo that something OUTSIDE it fetches by name.
A path listed here is load-bearing in a way `git grep` inside this repo cannot show you. Nothing
here imports `Sortable.min.js` by that name — but two other repos download it from GitHub by that
exact string at build time, and one of those builds is a production deploy. Move the file and this
repo stays green; someone else's deploy goes red, days later, in a log nobody is reading.
So: `test/public-paths.test.cjs` asserts every path below still exists. Moving one turns THIS
repo's CI red, on the commit that moved it, with the consumer named in the failure message.
🩸 WHY IT IS SHAPED THIS WAY. The first draft of this idea was a CONSUMERS.md — prose listing who
depends on us. It was withdrawn before it was written, because a list of facts about OTHER repos is
a list this repo cannot verify: it rots the moment a consumer changes, and it rots invisibly. What
is asserted below is the opposite — our OWN paths, which we can check on every push. The `namedBy`
lines are a hint for whoever gets the red, not the thing being tested. They may go stale. The paths
cannot, because a stale path is a failing test.
This list is one-directional and deliberately so. Being absent means 'nobody outside was known to
name this' — never 'safe to move'. It also covers only ONE mechanism: a path fetched by name. The
other is an absolute machine path hardcoded in some other checkout's source, which nothing in this
repo can see. Before moving anything, grep the other checkouts you have for the directory's path
as well — and note that a .gitignore-aware grep will hide exactly the copies that are running.
TO ADD an entry, say who names it and what breaks — an entry without both is a path with no claim
attached, and the test rejects it.

namedBy: CVERInc/reef  apps/mixfairy/modules/editor_backend/fetch-editor-assets.sh:139 — gh/curl contents API @ main, run at DYNO BOOT
CVERInc/ejecta  core/editor/fetch-tile-core.sh:26 — same fetch, into the web editor's vendor/
dist/editor-core.js.breaks: 🔴 NOT a red build — SILENT DEGRADATION IN PRODUCTION. Corrected 2026-08-12; the first version of this entry said 'mixfairy's Heroku build fails, so loudly', which described a build step that does not exist (there is no bin/post_compile). Measured: bootstrap.py:_boot_prep runs the fetch in a BACKGROUND asyncio task at dyno boot and catches every exception on purpose ('must never take the bot down'), logging 'editor UI assets will 404 until fixed (bot unaffected)'. So the bot stays up, the editor serves nothing, and only a log line says why. Worse: dl() is `gh api … | base64 --decode > $3`, and the redirect truncates the destination BEFORE the fetch fails — on any host with an existing static/, a 404 leaves a ZERO-BYTE file, which assets.py serves as 200 text/javascript. An empty module is not an error anyone sees.

hosts/obsidian/marktile/styles.css.breaks: Same silent degradation. Note both consumers RENAME it on arrival (to tile-core.css), so grepping them for 'styles.css' finds nothing — and `set -euo pipefail` means a failure on line 139 above kills this line too, so the blast radius of ONE renamed path is all three assets.

Sortable.min.js.breaks: Drag-to-reorder stops working. This one is the quietest of the three: it is loaded as a plain <script>, not a module, so a missing or empty file produces no console error at all — the handles simply do not drag.

packages/core/editor-core.js.breaks: nothing at build time — the banner is prose. It is here because the banner is the only record of where those generated files come from, and a rename makes it point at nothing
